director.chapterArc: A survivalist crossing where Jab assesses the flooded creek, rejects the river route due to time constraints, and attempts to cross on a fallen spruce tree while managing Tonk's trauma-induced panic. The scene escalates when the shoulder lashing snaps mid-crossing, forcing Jab into a precarious position where he must use his failing Kindling power to cut an obstruction before crawling across.
director.restraintNote: Maintain clinical precision during technical descriptions of the tree and repairs; allow physical exhaustion to permeate Jab's internal monologue without melodrama. The lashing snap should be delivered with quiet shock, not loud action. Tonk's dialogue remains factual but strained by fear.

cues.delivery: Jab speaks with protective warmth and absolute flatness to Tonk; no condescension. The reassurance is a tactical necessity.
cues.from: "Come here," Jab said, and put his forehead against his brother's forehead, which was all the holding you could do to a boy strapped into a frame. "Listen. I know. I know what it looks like. I'm going to tell you two things and they're both true."
cues.through: "Two is that I was carrying you when the bridge went," Jab said, "and I am still carrying you. Which means I'm the one who knows how to do this."
cues.reason: Dialogue shift from narrator observation to character interaction.

cues.delivery: Measured, rhythmic cadence mimicking the physical labor of stripping bark. Focus on tactile details.
cues.through: He tightened the hip belt to the fifth hole, which he had never used, so that the whole load sat as high and close to his spine as it would go. Then he put the hide over Tonk, and stopped, and took it off again. On any other ground he wanted his brother covered. On this ground he wanted to be able to see him.

cues.delivery: Sharp pacing shift at the snap. The sound is quiet; Jab's reaction is immediate physical realization.
cues.from: At the sag the spray started coming up over the wood, and he got four fingers over the handline and stopped talking. He had been talking the whole way, some nonsense about the alders on the far side, and he stopped because he needed everything.
cues.through: Then it stopped trying, because he had not let it, and the tree bounced twice under them and went still.
cues.reason: Critical turning point: failure of equipment.

cues.delivery: Struggle with the blade. The warmth is failing; Jab must force it open through sheer will and breath control.
cues.from: He put his hand flat in the air below it, and reached for the metal.
cues.through: He put the light out and let the metal go home before the shaking got into his hand.
cues.reason: Internal struggle with magical power under duress.

pauses.after: "Come here," Jab said, and put his forehead against his brother's forehead, which was all the holding you could do to a boy strapped into a frame. "Listen. I know. I know what it looks like. I'm going to tell you two things and they're both true."
pauses.reason: Speaker reset and emotional landing for Jab's reassurance to Tonk.

pauses.after: "Tonk." Jab put his hand on the side of his brother's face. His own hand was not steady and he did not bother hiding it, because the one thing he had refused to do for six weeks was lie to him about anything that mattered. "I'll come. That's not a promise about the water. That's a promise about me."
pauses.reason: Major emotional beat: Jab admitting his hand is shaking but promising he will come.

pauses.after: Ankle, thigh, seat, chest band, and then he checked every one of them again from the bottom, and then he checked the shoulder lashing where the boot-lace splint was, and it looked the way it had looked that morning — ugly, holding, three turns of lace over a cord that had gone to fur.
pauses.reason: Completed thought on the lashing condition before dialogue.
Emphasis on the specific failure point.

pauses.after: There was no warning in it at all. There was a small dull sound, a tick, no louder than a knuckle, and then the entire left side of the frame dropped two inches and everything above his hips swung.
pauses.reason: Major emotional landing: The snap and immediate physical consequence.

pauses.before: because he had not let it
pauses.reason: Highlighting Jab's agency in stopping the fall.
Pause for the failure of the blade to open; tension point.
Emphasis on the irony of timing for his power failure.

pauses.after: The leg had been jarred hard and twice. The wrapping had slipped and there was fresh clear wet on it, and the whole lower leg had gone tighter and hotter than it had been that morning, and Jab put his hands either side of it without touching and held them there and, for one bad moment, asked the thing in his chest the question he had promised himself he would only ask when he did not care about the answer.
pauses.reason: Major emotional landing: Jab realizing his power has failed him completely in a crisis.

pauses.before: asked the thing in his chest
pauses.reason: Isolating the desperate internal action before the silence of non-response.
Emphasis on the critical remaining supply count.
